description: kube's answer: contexts {contexts, where}; connect {sections, namespaces, nodes}; list {columns, rows, metrics, page}; yaml {text, file, refs}; owner {kind, name, resource}; summary {summary}; delete {said}; fault when a cluster can't be read; removed when its context has gone from the kubeconfig.

req.description: The request's number, the client's pick: its answers carry it back.

fault.description: The cluster can't be read: why.

removed.description: The context isn't in the kubeconfig (any more): nothing was read.

where.description: contexts: the kubeconfig files, or what stands for none.

sections.description: connect: the sidebar's categories, each kind with whether the cluster serves it.

nodes.description: connect: how many nodes it has.

page.description: list of a definition: its kind's page.

columns.description: list: the page's columns on this cluster.

metrics.description: list: whether CPU and memory could be read (pods, nodes), or null for another kind.

text.description: yaml: the YAML (a Secret's keys only, a Helm release's JSON).

file.description: yaml: what it is called, for its highlighting.

refs.description: yaml: the names in it that are other objects.

kind.description: owner: the controlling kind, climbed up from a ReplicaSet or a Job.

summary.description: summary: the stack's CPU and memory.

missing.description: kubectl isn't on the host: the Kubernetes view shows this in its place.
